name: Puraflo-G
description: A porous graphene oxide filtration membrane developed by BioForge Labs specifically for point-of-use water purification in low-infrastructure environments. Puraflo-G membranes use precisely controlled sub-nanometer pore geometries to reject dissolved heavy metals, biological contaminants, and industrial particulates while passing clean water at practical flow rates without pressurization. The membrane is produced in robust, field-replaceable cartridge formats designed to survive the rough handling of Shelf-level distribution.
story_hooks: The primary Puraflo-G supplier to three Shelf districts has begun quietly reducing membrane pore quality in replacement cartridges — clean water tests are passing on paper but long-term heavy metal accumulation is showing up in clinic data.

A BioForge Labs research note leaks suggesting Puraflo-G membranes can be modified to selectively filter out pharmaceutical compounds, meaning someone could use them to strip medication from a district's water supply.
Counterfeit Puraflo-G cartridges flooded the Shelf market after a supply disruption — they look identical but offer no meaningful filtration, and people are getting sick.
